spatialBenefitAssessment: The equal-count/unequal-remaining-work tie is a useful counterfactual beyond the recommended video, which switches policy on a fixed schedule. Height encodes meaningful work, but a viewpoint hiding height is not itself sufficient spatial discovery. The current run/pause sequence makes the critical tie easy to miss. A frozen dispatch decision with user-selected routing would make this a purposeful miniature investigation.

findings.issue: The claimed overhead counting view is obstructed by the worker presses, and the prescribed side view aligns the two lanes.
findings.requestedChange: Replace overhead press heads with side-mounted work indicators or open mechanisms so active request caps remain countable. Choose an oblique comparison view that separates A and B while showing both heights. Do not rely on hiding a dimension to manufacture discovery.
findings.evidence: build_scene.py places each 0.54-wide Press directly over the 0.4-wide active request at slot 0; the gantry beam also spans it. onPick side camera [9.5,1.6,-0.2] looks largely along the lanes’ X separation. Poster confirms substantial overhead structure; no alternate capture verifies readability.

findings.issue: The meaningful tie is buried in autoplay and captions describe the pre-service decision after service has already changed geometry.
findings.requestedChange: Replace Run/Pause with Advance one arrival and automatically hold before dispatch when counts tie but work differs. Keep policy as the second action. State the compared counts/work at that held decision, then advance service and update the caption to match the changed bars.
findings.evidence: tick records counts and before-work, routes and decrements remaining work, removes completed jobs, then publishes note. At the intended step-5 tie, caption refers to pre-step 4 versus 2 while settled rods have already shortened.

findings.issue: The count beam and press machinery add visual competition while request identities shrink with remaining work.
findings.requestedChange: Remove the decorative count balance unless it becomes the directly inspectable routing signal. Keep request identity on fixed-size bases separate from scaled work columns; use the spare space to enlarge the two lanes.
findings.evidence: Q labels are joined into each rod in build_scene.py, and interaction.js scales the entire rod on Y. The poster shows a separate balance, lever, arm and two gantries around a small six-request comparison.

findings.issue: Current camera and interaction behavior lack matching browser evidence.
findings.requestedChange: Capture the adjusted camera at 420px and desktop plus the equal-count tie and an idle-worker/queued-work state. Check visible mesh selection of both lanes and active requests; ensure click-to-view is optional and the key comparison is keyboard reachable.
findings.evidence: Only captures/initial.png is present and the user reports a subsequent camera adjustment; no alternate-state or post-adjustment capture establishes runtime framing. scene.json fallback also says one request is eight times taller than the rest despite Q4 having cost 3; change to eight times a unit-cost request.

requiredVerification: Run identical arrivals under each policy from Reset; independently check completion, short-request waits and idle-step totals against intent.json without treating those numbers as benchmarks.
At the held equal-count decision, verify counts include running and waiting requests, remaining heights match the caption, and switching policy never moves already assigned work.
Verify current GLB overhead and oblique views, pointer occlusion, 420px framing, reset mid-animation and reduced motion. No browser interaction or runtime tests were performed by this reviewer.
